precepts.text: Great is the Lord in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness; beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” The mountain of his holiness is Jerusalem.

“Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” This is the Zion that Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon: “Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities.” It is the city of the great King, the joy of the whole earth.

So the quiet habitation Isaiah saw is not a small thing. It is the city where the Lord is greatly praised, beautiful for situation, and it will never be taken down again.

precepts.text: They covet fields and take them by violence, and houses, and take them away, oppressing a man and his heritage.
precepts.point: The kingdom of heaven, the Israelites, suffered violence and the violent took it by force; Israel was taken out of the land by violence and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles until their time is fulfilled.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” Zion is the most sought after place on the earth, and that is why Esau always coveted the land: “And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.”

They covet fields and take them by violence, and houses, and take them away, oppressing a man and his heritage. Esau coveted Zion and told Babylon to raze it even to the foundation. The land was our heritage, and it was taken by violence.

precepts.text: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence and the violent take it by force.
precepts.point: The kingdom of heaven, the Israelites, suffered violence and the violent took it by force; Israel was taken out of the land by violence and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles until their time is fulfilled.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion”. Christ says what happened to it: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

The kingdom of heaven is the Israelites, and it suffered violence; the violent took it by force. Israel was taken out of the land by violence, the same violence Micah speaks of, coveting fields and taking them by violence. The city of the great King, beautiful for situation, was seized by the violent.

precepts.text: Israel shall fall by the edge of the sword and be led away captive into all nations, and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
precepts.point: The kingdom of heaven, the Israelites, suffered violence and the violent took it by force; Israel was taken out of the land by violence and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles until their time is fulfilled.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” That city is under the Gentiles now: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, and Jerusalem, the joy of the whole earth, is trodden down of the Gentiles. Esau coveted it and took it by violence, and he holds it only until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

precepts.text: Ye are the salt of the earth, and if the salt loses its savor it is good for nothing but to be cast out and trodden under foot; ye are the light of the world, a city set on a hill that cannot be hid.
precepts.point: The kings assembled, saw Zion, marveled, were troubled and hasted away; fear and pain took hold of them as of a woman in travail.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
Israel is the joy of the earth, the salt of the earth: “Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.”

You cannot make America great without the slaves, the strongest people on earth working for crumbs; that is the salt. Israel's savour is the commandments. Having lost the identity and the commandments, Israel became good for nothing but to be trodden under foot, only worth more when keeping the commandments and knowing the identity. Then Israel is the light of the world, the city set on a hill that cannot be hid, the city the kings saw and marvelled at.

precepts.text: Holofernes asked the princes of Moab and captains of Ammon who these people were, their cities, army, power and king.
precepts.point: The kings assembled, saw Zion, marveled, were troubled and hasted away; fear and pain took hold of them as of a woman in travail.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“For, lo, the kings were assembled, they passed by together. They saw it, and so they marvelled; they were troubled, and hasted away.” Judith shows that fear in the enemy. When Holofernes, the chief captain of the army of Assur, heard that the children of Israel “had prepared for war, and had shut up the passages of the hill country”, he “called all the princes of Moab, and the captains of Ammon, and all the governors of the sea coast” and asked, “Tell me now, ye sons of Chanaan, who this people is, that dwelleth in the hill country, and what are the cities that they inhabit, and what is the multitude of their army, and wherein is their power and strength, and what king is set over them, or captain of their army”.

The enemy did not know who this people was, what their power and strength were, or what king was set over them. When Israel was in rulership the nations fled and were afraid; they understood they could not come against Israel when the Most High was among them.

precepts.text: When Israel kept the commandments the nations could not overcome them lest they become a reproach before all the world.
precepts.point: The kings assembled, saw Zion, marveled, were troubled and hasted away; fear and pain took hold of them as of a woman in travail.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
The answer Holofernes got explains why the kings “were troubled, and hasted away”: “whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them. But when they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many battles very sore, and were led captives into a land that was not their’s”. So the counsel was, “if there be any error against this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them. But if there be no iniquity in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord defend them, and their God be for them, and we become a reproach before all the world.”

When Israel kept the commandments the nations could not overcome them, lest they become a reproach before all the world. That is the fear and pain “as of a woman in travail” that took hold of the kings. Israel's savour is the commandments; with them, the Most High is among us and the nations flee. Without them, Israel is good for nothing but to be trodden under foot.

precepts.text: There shall be signs in the sun, moon and stars, and upon the earth distress of nations with perplexity, men's hearts failing them for fear, for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.
precepts.point: While the nations are afraid Israel should gather together, get the pantry and the food and the house and the spirit in order, and rejoice rather than run around in fear.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“Let mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of thy judgments.” Israel is to rejoice when the Most High brings fear upon the nations, and Christ describes that fear: “there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.”

The nations are perplexed and in distress right now over the coronavirus, hearts failing them for fear. Israel with understanding is to be rejoicing that redemption draws near. While the nations are afraid, Israel should gather together, get the pantry and the food and the house and the spirit in order, and rejoice rather than run around in fear. “thy right hand is full of righteousness”, and his judgments are Zion's gladness.

precepts.text: You shall hear of wars and rumors of wars; see that ye be not troubled, for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
precepts.point: While the nations are afraid Israel should gather together, get the pantry and the food and the house and the spirit in order, and rejoice rather than run around in fear.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“Let mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of thy judgments.” While the nations fear, Christ tells Israel how to take it: “And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.”

See that ye be not troubled. The distress of the nations, the coronavirus, the hearts failing for fear: all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. So Israel does not run around in fear with the nations; we gather together, get the pantry and the food and the house and the spirit in order, and rejoice, because the Most High will establish Jerusalem for ever and his right hand is full of righteousness.

precepts.text: In the days of trouble the Most High delivers his beloved and guides them that keep his commandments.
precepts.point: The Most High led the teaching straight to that scripture; the Bible precepts link together because he leads his people to the places they need.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
Through Ezra the Most High speaks to his beloved: “Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.” The days of trouble are coming, but he delivers his own out of them. “Be ye not afraid neither doubt; for God is your guide”. That is the same promise David closes Psalm 48 with: “he will be our guide even unto death.” This God is our God for ever and ever, and he guides Israel through the trouble, so there is no cause to be afraid or to doubt.

He is “the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts”. The guiding is for the ones keeping his commandments; that is who walks about Zion, marks her bulwarks and tells it to the generation following. And he adds, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.”

The Most High led the teaching straight to this scripture. The Bible precepts link together like that, because he leads his people to the places they need.

precepts.text: According to His name, so is His praise unto the ends of the earth; His right hand is full of righteousness.
precepts.point: Moab is His washpot, the servant, and over Edom He casts out His shoe, treating Edom as a slave to clean His shoes.
precepts.why:
“save with thy right hand, and answer me.” Psalm 48 shows what the right hand is: “According to thy name, O God, so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.”

His right hand is full of righteousness, so the Israelites, his beloved, will be saved by keeping God's commandments. That is the saving with the right hand that David asks for.
